about.connect_2: In your wallet, add or edit the network and set its RPC URL to the address shown there, for example {url}.
about.connect_3: Use dApps as usual. Keep TxGate running; closing the window leaves it in the menu bar or system tray.
about.held_intro: These methods are held until you approve or reject them:
about.held_rest: Every other call is forwarded and shown under Requests.
about.intro: TxGate sits between your wallet and the RPC providers you choose. Reads are forwarded as they are. When the wallet estimates gas, which usually means it is about to ask you to sign, TxGate decodes the transaction and highlights it. When the wallet sends a signed transaction, TxGate holds it. Nothing reaches the network until you have read it here and approved it.
about.limit_decide: Approving or rejecting is all TxGate can do. A signed transaction cannot be changed.
about.limit_direct: If the wallet sends directly to its own servers instead of the configured RPC, TxGate never sees the transaction.
about.limit_safe: Safe owners approve transactions by signing typed data, which TxGate cannot see either. Check each one on the Safe multisig page before you sign, and compare the hashes there with your signing device.
about.limit_simulation: Simulation shows what would happen at the current block. The outcome can differ when the transaction is mined.
about.signatures: Signature requests never pass through the RPC. Messages signed with personal_sign or eth_signTypedData, including Permit, Permit2 and marketplace listings, are signed inside your wallet and handed straight to the website. A malicious site can use such a signature to move your tokens without any transaction from you. TxGate cannot warn you about these. Read every signature request in your wallet with the same care.

safepage.check_intro: Safe signatures go from your wallet straight to the signing device, so TxGate never sees them. Paste what you are about to sign and TxGate decodes it, reads the Safe from your own upstream and computes the hashes. Sign only if the hashes on your device match.

safepage.intro: Transactions a Safe executes through TxGate are decoded and checked automatically. This page covers what TxGate cannot see: the signatures themselves, and activity on the Safe that you did not start.

safepage.watched_intro: Every {secs} seconds TxGate reads each Safe and alerts you when its owners, threshold, implementation, guard, fallback handler or modules change, and when someone proposes a new transaction. Proposals are re-hashed and decoded locally; the Safe Transaction Service is not trusted.
